This page tracks that timeline and, once a lockout starts, how long it has run — updated from one small public data file, not a prediction of how talks end.

What's being negotiated

The Basic Agreement is the contract between MLB's 30 clubs and the players' union (the MLBPA) that governs pay, free agency, arbitration, roster rules and more. Based on public reporting as talks continue, the clubs have proposed a salary cap paired with a minimum payroll floor, and the union has rejected a cap while pushing for a higher minimum salary and other player-side gains. Other reported topics include the length of the regular season and playoff format. None of this is final — it is what has been reported, not an agreement.

Lockout vs. strike, and the key dates

A lockout is management shutting the business down and barring players from club facilities; a strike is players refusing to work. The 2021-22 stoppage was a lockout: it began December 2, 2021 and ran 99 days, ending March 10, 2022. Opening Day moved from March 31 to April 7, but the sides later agreed to play a full 162-game season anyway, so no games were ultimately missed. The current agreement expires December 1, 2026.

How a lockout affects service time, Super Two and arbitration

No service time accrues on days no games are played — the clock only moves while a player is on a major league roster. In 2021-22, the eventual deal restored a full 162-game season, so no player's service time or free-agency timeline ended up shorter for it; that is public history, not a guarantee about any future lockout. A lockout has historically pushed back offseason business broadly, including salary arbitration scheduling and tender deadlines, and it has no effect on the Super Two rule's mechanics themselves — only on how much of a season there ends up being to measure it against.

Minor league options, free agency and transactions

During a lockout, clubs cannot sign free agents, make trades, or complete other transactions involving players on a 40-man roster — business involving players not on a 40-man roster, including most minor league option moves, is generally unaffected. See who's arbitration-eligible this winter for the group whose contracts are usually decided right around when a lockout would hit.

FAQ

Does service time accrue during an MLB lockout?

No. A player only earns a day of major league service time for a day spent on a major league roster, and a lockout freezes that entirely — there is no roster to be on. Time already earned before a lockout is never taken away; it simply stops adding up until play resumes.

What's the difference between a lockout and a strike?

A lockout is called by the owners, who shut business down and bar players from club facilities. A strike is called by the players, who refuse to work. The 2021-22 work stoppage was a lockout; earlier disputes in MLB history, including the 1994-95 stoppage, were players' strikes.

When does the current CBA expire, and when could a lockout start?

The agreement expires December 1, 2026. In the last round of bargaining, owners locked players out within a day of the old deal expiring, so a similar timeline is widely expected again if no new agreement is reached first.

Are free-agent signings and trades frozen during a lockout?

Yes, for any player on a 40-man roster. Clubs cannot sign free agents, make trades, or complete other 40-man transactions while a lockout is in effect, which is why free-agent activity typically rushes to beat the deadline.

Does a lockout affect salary arbitration or minor league options?

A lockout halts the business side of the sport broadly, which has historically pushed back tender deadlines and arbitration-related scheduling along with everything else. Minor league option rules themselves are unaffected by a lockout — see our service time explainer for how options interact with the clock.

How long did the last MLB lockout last?

99 days: it began December 2, 2021 and ended March 10, 2022. Opening Day moved from March 31 to April 7, but the two sides agreed to play a full 162-game season on a compressed schedule, so no games were ultimately missed.
